A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MrSteve research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching renamed methods and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Minecraft exploration, sequential-task, memory-constrained navigation, and long-horizon experiments, alongside appendix ablations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds planning-task evaluations, task-conditioned exploration experiments, memory-capacity sweeps, and memory-compression comparisons.

M1.justification: The original controller remains, but v3 adds two substantive implemented alternatives. Appendix N introduces task-conditioned exploration using semantic relevance maps and spatial smoothing. Appendix P introduces PEM that discards individual frame embeddings after clustering and retains cluster centers, changing storage and retrieval.

E1.justification: Appendix M extends evaluation from resource collection and navigation to multi-step crafting and planning. Table 10 evaluates eleven tasks with ground-truth plans, while Table 9 evaluates four with an LLM-based DEPS planner. These introduce task requirements absent from v1.

E2.justification: Appendix P adds the center-embedding-only memory variant to the ABA-Sparse comparison, and Appendix N compares task-conditioned and task-free exploration. Existing external baselines remain; STEVE-FM/EM/PM becoming MrSteve-FM/EM/PM are renamings. Applying the retained Steve-1 comparator to planning tasks does not itself add a baseline.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include LLM-generated versus ground-truth plans, task-specific 3,000/6,000-step budgets, and memory capacities from 100 to 12,000 frames. Appendix N additionally measures exploration-mode duration and pasture visitation over time. The settings documented for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing navigation and memory-hyperparameter ablations, v3 tests whether semantic task conditioning improves exploration, whether memory performance survives capacity restrictions, and whether retaining only cluster centers reduces redundancy without sacrificing success. Ground-truth-plan controls also examine controller performance without LLM planning errors.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2.1 retains 100 episodes with different seeds and five runs for the original long-horizon tasks. Standard-error reporting was already present in v1. The additions use that reporting practice without documenting increased repetitions or new statistical procedures; planning success rates have no accompanying uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear in Tables 9–11 and Figures 16–18. For bed, newly reported success rates are 50% versus 27% with DEPS and 60% versus 37% with ground-truth plans, favoring MrSteve; ground-truth sign instead favors Steve-1, 70% versus 67%. Table 11 reports shorter exploration durations, including 1202.64 versus 1512.00 steps for Beef-Log-Beef. These are added comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1 results.

T1.justification: Appendix M adds formal plan/subgoal notation and the horizon-prediction-based selection distribution in Equation 3. Existing memory-complexity reasoning and navigator equations remain substantively unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about episodic-memory limitations, PEM, memory-guided exploration, and improved task solving. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine those main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the untested LLM-integration limitation with the narrower limitation that high-level planners cannot access PEM. New discussion explains task-relevant exploration and the storage-efficiency versus task-success tradeoff of retaining cluster centers. Existing terrain and positional-information limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly specifies the existing DP-Means penalty as delta = 1 and explains initialization. New appendices document Qwen2.5-72B, heuristic crafting actions, exploration prompts, spatial smoothing, and compressed-memory handling. These extend reproducibility information; the original hardware, training details, and code-release statements are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to GPT-4, CLIP, and Qwen2.5, including repairing the unresolved introduction citation. The main positioning against planner-oriented memory systems remains unchanged. Updated bibliographic details for already cited works do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes agent and variant names, changes observation notation, expands MineCLIP and DP-Means explanations, and revises the limitations paragraph. Appendices M–P are appended without substantial reorganization of the existing narrative. The conclusion also acquires a duplicated opening clause.

P2.justification: Tables 8–11 and Figures 16–18 substantially expand the visual presentation with planning comparisons, exploration trajectories, memory-capacity curves, and compression results. Existing plots also receive revised legends, fonts, and colors. Earlier tables and figures remain identifiable despite pagination changes.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly left LLM-planner integration untested despite motivating the work through hierarchical-controller bottlenecks. Appendix M addresses this gap with DEPS comparisons and ground-truth-plan controls, while Appendices O–P strengthen evidence about memory capacity and efficiency tradeoffs. Together these substantially improve support for the paper's central rationale. Planning results still lack uncertainty estimates, and compressed memory has notable task-specific losses, limiting broader claims.
